### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **3** package(s): `@objectstack/cli`, `@objectstack/plugin-audit`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **161** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **6** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/plugins/plugin-audit/src/audit-seal/index.ts`, `packages/plugins/plugin-audit/src/index.ts`, `packages/plugins/plugin-audit/src/objects/index.ts`, …), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**61** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 33bad96192fe929916ac068f84c32abcf6207180`.

⛔ **16** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **6** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/plugins/plugin-audit/src/audit-seal/index.ts`, `packages/plugins/plugin-audit/src/index.ts`, `packages/plugins/plugin-audit/src/objects/index.ts`, …) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **1** cross-cutting symbol(s) contributed no route anchor: `isSystem (5 routes)`
- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `created_at (literal, 43 pages)`
- **23** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **231** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **166** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **166**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **107** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **183** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 33bad96192fe929916ac068f84c32abcf6207180` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `df5e1155e360c4cde51fd6cd109704f14f442509` — the merge of head `423407419085518fac74efa7795433119aea5b81` into base `33bad96192fe929916ac068f84c32abcf6207180`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin df5e1155e360c4cde51fd6cd109704f14f442509 && git checkout df5e1155e360c4cde51fd6cd109704f14f442509
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 33bad96192fe929916ac068f84c32abcf6207180 423407419085518fac74efa7795433119aea5b81 && git checkout -B drift-repro 33bad96192fe929916ac068f84c32abcf6207180 && git merge --no-ff 423407419085518fac74efa7795433119aea5b81

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 33bad96192fe929916ac068f84c32abcf6207180
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 33bad96192fe929916ac068f84c32abcf6207180` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `423407419085518fac74efa7795433119aea5b81`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/contracts/audit-checkpoint.ts, packages/spec/src/contracts/crypto-provider.ts, packages/spec/src/contracts/index.ts + packages/plugins/plugin-audit/src/audit-seal/jcs.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-audit/src/audit-seal/canonical.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-audit/src/audit-seal/seed.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-audit/src/audit-seal/merkle.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-audit/src/audit-seal/signed-body.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-audit/src/audit-seal/index.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-audit/src/index.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-audit/src/objects/index.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-audit/src/objects/sys-audit-checkpoint.object.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-audit/src/objects/sys-audit-amendment.object.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-audit/src/objects/sys-audit-signing-key.object.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-audit/src/audit-writers.ts, packages/cli/src/utils/secret-reference-union.ts, packages/cli/src/utils/sys-secret-rewrap.ts, packages/cli/src/utils/sys-secret-orphan-sweep.ts, packages/cli/src/commands/secret/rewrap.ts

Read for this record: card #31908 with every comment (claim 6759393778, amendments 6759503769 and 6762115714, dev reports 6761943000 and 6762979157), the seat's rulings file, the PR body and file list, the net diff against merge-base `c0abfb7df3`, ADR-0154 on `main`, and the check-runs on this head. Code outside the diff was read only to judge (`LocalCryptoProvider`, the rewrap executor, the orphan-sweep planner, `sys_secret`, `sys_audit_log`, `platform-object-names.ts` and its test). Everything else in the diff (tests, `api-surface`, `export-origins`, the tenancy census, the changeset text) is the lane seat's ACCEPT at `TIER_DEFAULT`. There is no `rotateKey` provider change in the diff: the only provider change is a test pin in service-settings.

**CI on this head: RED.** `Test Core (2/8)` and the aggregate `Test Core` concluded `failure`; every other check-run is `success` or `skipped`. The failure is caused by this diff, see M1.

### ① Derived judgments

1. **`@objectstack/spec` contracts gain six names: right.** `AUDIT_CHECKPOINT_SIGNER_SERVICE`, `AUDIT_CHECKPOINT_SINK_SERVICE`, `AuditCheckpointSignature`, `AuditCheckpointSinkEntry`, `IAuditCheckpointSigner`, `IAuditCheckpointSink`. `api-surface/contracts.json` adds exactly these six. Two are ADR-0154's table, four are ruled in amendment 6762115714. The slot values `audit.checkpointSigner` and `audit.checkpointSink` match D11.
2. **`CRYPTO_CONTEXT_SCOPES` gains `audit_seal`: right, a widening.** `LocalCryptoProvider.requireScope` reads the constant, so the shipped provider accepts the scope with no code change. The union type `CryptoContextScope` widens too, which stops an exhaustive `Record` over it from compiling. The one in-tree case (`rewrapByScope` in `sys-secret-rewrap.ts`) is now derived from the constant. An out-of-tree provider with such a record is a `carrier: cloud` note.
3. **The `rotateKey` MUST: right, and not a narrowing.** It binds only the new scope, which no provider could be called with before this change. The SHOULD for the other three scopes is word for word as on `main`.
4. **`@objectstack/plugin-audit` root gains four named exports and no star export: right.** `AUDIT_SEAL_SECRET_HOLDERS`, `checkpointSeedContext`, `isAuditSealSecretCoordinate`, `signingKeyContext`. The root has no `export *`, the package exports only `.`, and the three objects and the rest of `src/audit-seal/` are not reachable from it. These four are not in the amendment's list of ruled names. They are covered by its file-surface line ("named exports only, limited to what is used outside the package"), and all four are read by `secret-reference-union.ts`. The seat should confirm them by name when it posts this record.
5. **cli: right.** `SECRET_REFERENCE_FAMILIES` gains `audit-seal` (a ruled name), `SCOPE_OF_HOLDER_FAMILY` maps it to `audit_seal`, and the rewrap report's `rewrapByScope` and every `families` map gain a member. All additive.
6. **`AUDIT_EXCLUDED_OBJECTS` gains three names: right.** D4 names exactly this set. The names carry the reserved `sys_` prefix and nothing registers them on `main`, so nothing audited today stops being audited. The diff of `audit-writers.ts` is the set literal and its comment only, as the claim requires.
7. **Three object definitions under `src/objects/`: WRONG as landed.** They are declared in a platform package but `PLATFORM_OBJECTS_BY_PACKAGE['plugin-audit']` in `packages/spec/src/system/constants/platform-object-names.ts` was not updated, and the spec's own conformance test fails on it (M1). The tenancy census was regenerated for the same three files, so the diff treats them as platform objects in one register and not in the other.
8. **No authorable key, no `packages/spec/src/data/**`, no `docs/adr/**` in the diff: right.** Both stop conditions of the claim hold.

### ② Semver level

- `Clause-②: yes (widening)` and `Metadata-protocol: none` are on the PR body and in the changeset body, in the same words as amendment 6759503769. `Check Changeset` and `PR-body guards` are `success` on this head, and those are the gates that read the two lines through `scripts/pm/clause2-line.mjs`.
- The reading is correct on the tree: every change in ① is additive, and the diff adds no key an author writes.
- The changeset is `patch` for `@objectstack/spec`, `@objectstack/plugin-audit` and `@objectstack/cli`, which is the level `Metadata-protocol: none` gives. service-settings has a test-only change and no entry: right.
- `Part of #31908` is on the PR body, as ruled for P1a.
- should-fix S5 below: the changeset says the three objects "are exported". They are not exported from the package root, so a reader of the CHANGELOG cannot import them.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Files outside the first P1a surface** (`sys-secret-orphan-sweep.ts`, `commands/secret/rewrap.ts`, `plugin-audit/src/index.ts`, the tenancy census): accepted, each is named in amendment 6762115714 and in the PR body. One correction for the seat: the amendment describes `sys-secret-orphan-sweep.ts` as carrying "the fourth reference family's unregistered-holder rule". It does not. Its diff is the family count in one refusal message and one doc word. The rule lives in `secret-reference-union.ts#collectAuditSealSecretReferences`, which is where this record reviewed it.
- **Forced test files outside the claim:** the lane seat's ACCEPT at `TIER_DEFAULT`, not judged here.
- **Translations deferred to P1b:** accepted. The objects are registered on no runtime in this slice.
- **Ruling 3d's pin deferred to P1b:** accepted. It needs the sealer. This slice pins only the exclusion.
- **Ruling 3c's check that `chain_key` agrees with `tenant_id`:** it belongs to verify (P2). This slice gives it the one function to check against (`chainKeyOf`). Carried, not owed here.
- **Open question, cloud KMS `rotateKey` pin:** option A is right. The seat already ruled out-of-tree providers `carrier: cloud`, and the PR body's Acceptance notes say so. The same carrier note should mention the widened `CryptoContextScope` (① item 2).
- **Open question, `canonicalValue` number and JSON pass-through:** option A in P1b is right, and it must land in the same PR as `lifecycle.seal`, because that key is what lets a second object opt in. Read on the tree: `sys_audit_log` declares no number, boolean or JSON column, so nothing passes through unnormalised for the one object that will seal by default. The question is wider than the dev states it: every type other than `date`, `datetime` and `boolean` passes through as the driver returned it, so P1b should either normalise each declared type or refuse to seal an object that declares a clear column of a type with no rule.
- **New flag, escalated to the seat (M1):** the fix touches `packages/spec/src/system/constants/platform-object-names.ts`, a published spec file outside the claimed surface. The seat amends the claim, or rules that the three object files move to P1b with their registration.

### ④ Design judgment

**must-fix**

- **M1. The spec's platform-object registry is out of date, and CI is red on it.** `@objectstack/spec#test:repo` fails in `Test Core (2/8)`: `platform-object-names.test.ts`, "registers exactly the objects each package declares", reports `registry group "plugin-audit" is out of date` with `sys_audit_amendment`, `sys_audit_checkpoint` and `sys_audit_signing_key` missing. The test scans every `*.object.ts` under `packages/`, and the registry's own header states the rule: "adding an object to a platform package means adding its name here". Fix: add the three names to `PLATFORM_OBJECTS_BY_PACKAGE['plugin-audit']` under a seat amendment (it changes the value of the public `PLATFORM_PROVIDED_OBJECT_NAMES`, additively), or move the three object files to P1b. The dev report's "106 gates, all 0" did not run this suite, and CI was not awaited.

**should-fix**

- **S1. `IAuditCheckpointSigner.sign` and the signed body disagree on who names the key first** (`audit-checkpoint.ts` against `signed-body.ts`). D4 puts `signing_key_id` inside the signed bytes, and `CheckpointSignedBody` does. The contract hands the key id back only with the signature and says it is "never asked for separately". So the sealer must put a key id into the bytes before it knows which key will sign, and after a rotation `sign()` can return a `keyId` that differs from the one the bytes name. Such a row would never verify. The ruled shape can stay. The contract must state the caller's duty: compare the returned `keyId` with the one in the bytes, and rebuild and sign again when they differ. P1b pins that loop.
- **S2. `AuditCheckpointSinkEntry.body` understates what a sink receives.** The jsdoc says "only commitments, roots, digests and handle ids". The body built in `signed-body.ts` also carries `tenant_id`, every sealed row id (`row_ids`), the window instants and the column names. None of these is a value, a salt, a seed or key material, so D2 holds, but a stage-2 sink author classifies data from this sentence. Name the organization id and row ids.
- **S3. A redaction amendment signs `checkpoint_id`, which is neither signed in the checkpoint nor handed to the sink.** `id` is outside `CheckpointSignedBody`, and `AuditCheckpointSinkEntry` carries the body only. An off-host copy therefore cannot resolve the reference, and on the host it resolves through a column anyone with database access can rewrite. It is not a forgery path: `row_id` is signed, and a verifier can require it in the named checkpoint's `row_ids`. Before P3 writes the first amendment, reference the checkpoint by something signed and exported (its `sequence`, or its digest). The objects are registered nowhere yet, so the change is free now.
- **S4. `crypto-provider.ts` is half updated.** The header says four producers. The `CryptoContext` doc still says "the three producer vocabularies share it", and the `namespace` and `key` member docs list three producers. Add the audit-seal coordinates, and say there that this producer passes no `tenantId` (ruling Q7), since a provider author reads that paragraph.
- **S5. The changeset says the three objects "are exported".** They are exported from `src/objects/index.ts` only. Say "defined, not yet registered".

**nit**

- `isAuditSealSecretCoordinate` can throw instead of answering `false`: a `key` that parses to an array whose first member holds an unpaired surrogate makes `canonicalJson` throw, and `collectAuditSealSecretReferences` calls the predicate outside its `try`. The command fails closed (nothing is deleted or re-wrapped), but the family should report a gap.
- `jcs.ts` builds its error path from member names. For a leaf these are column names. For a committed JSON value they would be the payload's own keys. Decide with the P1b normaliser.
- `nullableText` reads an absent `tenant_id` as the deployment chain. A projection that drops the column fails loudly at the signature, so it is safe, but a refusal would be clearer.
- `auditSealMintedPair` turns an empty-string `sequence` into 0. It only affects the placement report.
- `sys-secret.object.ts` (outside the diff) still says "three privileged producers". Update it in P1b with the producer.
- `canonicalDatetime` reads a number as epoch milliseconds and refuses digits-as-text. Both are the loud direction. State the unit in the jsdoc.

**What holds, file by file**

- **`audit-checkpoint.ts` (hits).** Slots and interface names are D11's. `sign()` returns `{ keyId, signature }` and `trustedPublicKey(keyId)` returns a vouched key or `null`, as ruled in §6. On D6: the doc forbids trusting a key because a row carries it and binds the local signer to the wrapped private half. A caller can take a `keyId` from a row, but gets a public key back only when the signer vouches for it, so the row alone never confers trust. The doc ties the method to the live check, which agrees with the ruling that `--bundle` never calls the signer. `deliver()` receives `kind`, the signed body, `keyId` and `signature`. `body` is typed as an open record, so the type cannot exclude a seed. What excludes it is `signed-body.ts`, whose two body shapes have no field for a seed, a salt or a private key: `seed_handle` is a `sys_secret` row id. P1b must pass the sink only the output of `checkpointBodyFromRow` or `amendmentBodyFromRow`.
- **`crypto-provider.ts` (hits).** The MUST is limited to `audit_seal` in both places it is stated. The only in-tree `ICryptoProvider` is `LocalCryptoProvider`, whose `rotateKey` returns `id: handle.id` for every scope. The rewrap writer updates by `sys_secret.id` and `resealHolds` refuses a re-seal whose id moved, before any write. D2's requirement is met on every in-tree path.
- **`contracts/index.ts` (hits).** One star re-export of the new file, the pattern of its neighbours.
- **`jcs.ts`.** RFC 8785: numbers and strings through `JSON.stringify`, members sorted by UTF-16 code units, no whitespace, unpaired surrogates refused, anything non-JSON refused instead of coerced. No error carries a value.
- **`canonical.ts`.** Datetime is `toISOString()` (UTC, milliseconds), zoneless SQL text read as UTC, `date` handled before `datetime`. Commitment is `SHA-256(salt ‖ JCS(v))` with absent and null committed alike. Leaf hash is `SHA-256(0x00 ‖ JCS(leaf))`. Order is canonical `created_at`, then id, by code units. All as D1 says. Refusals name the row id, the column and the type, never the value.
- **`seed.ts`.** 32-byte seed. Salt is `HMAC-SHA-256(seed, utf8(object) ‖ 0x00 ‖ utf8(id) ‖ 0x00 ‖ utf8(column))`, built in one buffer. The encoding is unambiguous while object and column names hold no NUL, which the naming rules give. The seed context is scope `audit_seal`, namespace the sealed object, key `JCS([tenantIdOrNull, sequence])`, no `tenantId`: D2 and ruling Q7. The signing-key context uses the fingerprint as its key: D6.
- **`merkle.ts`.** Node hash `SHA-256(0x01 ‖ left ‖ right)`, pairwise levels, odd last node promoted unchanged, no root of zero leaves. This yields the same root as RFC 6962's split for every leaf count, and `leaf_count` is under the signature.
- **`signed-body.ts`.** The checkpoint body carries every field D4 lists and nothing else. `id`, `chain_key` and `signature` are outside it. `tenant_id` stays NULL for the deployment chain, and `chainKeyOf` is injective (`deployment` against `org:` plus the id). Checkpoint kinds and amendment kinds are disjoint, so a signature over one kind of body cannot be replayed as the other. The amendment bodies carry what D7 and D8 list, with the policy value under the signature.
- **The three objects.** Names from ADR-0154's table. `append-only`, private by default, `get` and `list` only, deployment-level. The unique index is `(sealed_object, chain_key, sequence)` as ruled in 3c. Columns match the body fields one for one.
- **`secret-reference-union.ts`, `sys-secret-rewrap.ts`, `sys-secret-orphan-sweep.ts`.** With both holders registered, every handle arrives with its minted pair. With a holder unregistered, the family is enumerated and empty when no `sys_secret` row carries an audit-seal coordinate, and a gap when one does: ruling 3a, both sides. Rewrap opens each row under `{ scope, namespace, key }` with no `tenantId`, which is exactly the context the producer seals under. **Can an orphan sweep delete a seed or a signing key? No.** A row is deletable only when the union is complete, no family references it, and its `(namespace, key)` matches a registered encrypted settings specifier. A referenced seed is `referenced`. An unreferenced one is `unattributable`, which the sweep never deletes. Evidence without a readable holder is a gap, which empties the deletable set.
- **Error messages.** No refusal in the scoped files carries a raw value. Gap reasons carry counts and object names.
